newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Tapie hangs on at Euro-Parliament.
newsitem.headline: France's Tapie hangs on at Euro-Parliament.

text.p: Controversial French businessman and soccer boss Bernard Tapie won a reprieve on Monday when the European Parliament deferred a decision to strip him of his seat.
But his days in the Strasbourg-based assembly are numbered, parliamentary officials said during a closed-door meeting of deputies overseeing proper application of the rules.

France announced at the end of October it was stripping Tapie of his seat, but his lawyers appealed against the decision, unprecedented in the history of the European parliament, and a situation not provided for in its rules.

French deputy Thierry Jean-Pierre -- one of the key judges who fought against alleged corruption in the French socialist party -- said deputies felt it was premature to throw him out until the appeals procedure had run its full course.
Jean-Pierre said Tapie had promised him personally to resign the moment the French Supreme Court confirms his sentence for match-rigging at the Olympique Marseille soccer team he once ran.
Tapie has already been ejected from the French National Assembly (the lower house) under a court ruling upheld by the Supreme Court declaring him to be bankrupt and ineligible for public office.

Tapie, the target of a blizzard of legal actions over his now destroyed business empire and the Marseille soccer team, has been sentenced to jail terms of eight and six months for tax fraud and rigging a soccer match.
He is appealing both cases in the supreme court.
He showed clear irritation at the presence of reporters when he arrived to be heard by the Parliament's rules committee, but emerged looking relieved.
